name: read.zoo
title: Read a zoo series from a table

origin.description: Read a text file and return a zoo series. This is the zoo 1.9-1 reader.
origin.usage:
read.zoo(file, format = "", tz = "", FUN = NULL,
  regular = FALSE, index.column = 1, drop = TRUE, FUN2 = NULL,
  split = NULL, aggregate = FALSE, ..., text, read = read.table)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path, text connection, or data frame to read. Several paths are read and merged.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: Date format passed to FUN. Omitted means missing, which is not the same as an empty string.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: Time zone passed to as.POSIXct. Omitted means missing. An empty string is the local zone.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Function that builds the index from index.column. NULL chooses numeric, Date, or POSIXct.

arguments.name: regular
arguments.text: If TRUE and the series is regular, coerce it to zooreg.

arguments.name: index.column
arguments.text: Column number, name, or list of columns that hold the index. 0 uses the row names. The default is 1.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: If TRUE, a single data column is returned as a vector.

arguments.name: FUN2
arguments.text: Applied to the index after FUN. If FUN is omitted, only FUN2 runs.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: Column used to split long data into separate series. Inf and -Inf number the runs.

arguments.name: aggregate
arguments.text: FALSE keeps duplicate indexes. TRUE averages them. Any other function aggregates each index.
Further arguments passed to read, unless file is already a data frame.

arguments.name: text
arguments.text: Character data read through a text connection when file is omitted.

arguments.name: read
arguments.text: Reader for file. The default is read.table.

origin.details: read.zoo reads the file with read.table unless read= selects another reader or file is already a data frame. The index.column (default the first) becomes the index and the other columns become the data. When FUN is omitted, a numeric index stays numeric. A character index is POSIXct when tz is supplied, Date when format is supplied, and otherwise a heuristic: POSIXct, then Date when every time is the same clock time. An omitted format or tz is missing. An explicit empty string is not missing.
origin.value: An object of class "zoo", or "zooreg" when regular is TRUE and the series is regular.
origin.example:
.libPaths(c(path.expand("~/R/library"), .libPaths()))
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(zoo))
path <- tempfile()
writeLines(c(
  "date,a,b",
  "2020-01-01,1.5,2.25",
  "2020-01-02,3.5,4.75",
  "2020-01-03,5.25,6.125"
), path)
z <- read.zoo(path, header = TRUE, sep = ",")
cat(sprintf("index %s\n", paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.numeric(index(z))), collapse = " ")))
cat(sprintf("values %s\n", paste(sprintf("%.17g", as.vector(coredata(z))), collapse = " ")))

translation.description: Python read_zoo returns a Zoo. The core data is a NumPy array.
translation.usage:
read_zoo(file, format=MISSING, tz=MISSING, FUN=None,
  regular=False, index_column=1, drop=True, FUN2=None,
  split=None, aggregate=False, *, text=MISSING, read=None, **kwargs)

arguments.name: file
arguments.text: Path or text. A DataFrame is used as the table and is not read again.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: Date format. Omit it to leave the argument missing. An explicit empty string is supplied.

arguments.name: tz
arguments.text: Time zone. Omit it to leave the argument missing. "" is the local zone and selects POSIXct when it is supplied.

arguments.name: FUN
arguments.text: Callable or name such as "as.Date" that builds the index. None selects the heuristic.

arguments.name: regular
arguments.text: When True and the index has a constant positive step, the series is marked regular.

arguments.name: index_column
arguments.text: 1-based column number, name, or list of columns. 0 uses the row names.

arguments.name: drop
arguments.text: When True, one data column is stored as a 1-d NumPy array.

arguments.name: FUN2
arguments.text: Called on the index after FUN.

arguments.name: split
arguments.text: Column that splits long data. math.inf numbers each run from the start.

arguments.name: aggregate
arguments.text: False keeps every row. True averages duplicate indexes.

arguments.name: text
arguments.text: String read when file is omitted.

arguments.name: read
arguments.text: Callable used to read a path. The default is read_table.

arguments.name: **kwargs
arguments.text: Passed to read. Ignored when file is already a data frame.

translation.details: The table is read with the Python csv rules for comma, semicolon, and tab files, and with a whitespace splitter for read.table. Values are a NumPy array in Fortran order. A character index such as 2020-01-01 becomes datetime.date when format and tz are omitted. read_table_zoo passes format="" and tz="", so this heuristic is not the one that runs.
translation.value: A Zoo. index is datetime.date, datetime.datetime, or a numeric NumPy array. data holds the series.
translation.example:
import datetime as dt
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

sys.path.insert(0, "/home/ahmed/killr_projects/killr/packages/zoo")
from zoo.io import read_zoo

path = tempfile.mktemp()
Path(path).write_text(
    "date,a,b\n"
    "2020-01-01,1.5,2.25\n"
    "2020-01-02,3.5,4.75\n"
    "2020-01-03,5.25,6.125\n"
)
z = read_zoo(path, header=True, sep=",")
origin = dt.date(1970, 1, 1)
print("index " + " ".join(format(float((value - origin).days), ".17g") for value in z.index))
print("values " + " ".join(format(float(value), ".17g") for value in np.asarray(z.data, dtype=float).ravel(order="F")))
